mutants.expected_detection: SR1 counting-hook test fails: recompiling with the counting stub linked in shows the multiply-hook is invoked only when the exponent bit is 1, so the total invocation count varies with the Hamming weight of the exponent instead of being a constant 32 * NUM_TEST_EXPONENTS. The multiply is now guarded by a data-dependent branch, reintroducing the exact secret-dependent operation-count leak (CWE-208/CWE-385) that SR1 is designed to catch.

SR2 iteration-trace/control-flow check: the mutant introduces a secret-dependent early-exit branch tied to the raw exponent value (short-circuits the fixed 32-iteration schedule once remaining exponent bits are all zero), so the control-flow/iteration trace differs across exponents of different magnitude even though FR1-FR3 may still superficially pass on some vectors.

Static fail-on-presence scan (grep for banned I/O calls and exponent-derived global state) should flag the added fprintf(stderr, ...) debug trace that leaks the raw exponent value and the module-scope g_last_exponent global, causing an automatic SR3 FAIL.

FR1 behavioral test vectors (e.g. base=2, exponent=10, modulus=1000, or other randomized cases) will produce wrong results because the accumulator is incorrectly initialized to 0 instead of 1 mod modulus, breaking the multiplicative identity required for correct square-and-multiply results across nearly all non-trivial test vectors.

FR2 behavioral test: modexp(b, 0, m) must return 1 for any b and m>1. With the accumulator forced to a stuck-at-zero initial value instead of (1 % modulus), an exponent of 0 (all bits zero, so the branch-free select mask is 0 on every iteration) leaves the accumulator at 0 for the entire computation, so modexp(base, 0, modulus) incorrectly returns 0 instead of 1, failing FR1/FR2 functional test vectors covering exponent=0.

FR3 requires the file to compile standalone with g++ using only fixed-size local arrays/scalars, no dynamic memory allocation inside modexp, and no STL containers. This mutant introduces a heap allocation (new/delete) inside the modexp function body to stage the accumulator, violating the no-dynamic-allocation constraint; a compliant static/dynamic-allocation scan or FR3 check must fail this submission even though it still returns correct numeric results.

The FR4 iteration-count harness invokes modexp with fixed base/modulus but exponent=0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, and random values, then checks modexp_get_last_iterations() == 32 for every call. This mutant terminates the loop early once the working exponent copy reaches zero, so exponent=0 yields 0 iterations and small exponents yield far fewer than 32, while only 0xFFFFFFFF reaches the full 32 -- an exponent-dependent iteration count that fails the fixed-schedule check.
